claim: Nanoparticles disperse throughout coral tissues via the paracellular pathway after entering the general coelenteric cavity.
source: After entering the general coelenteric cavity, we show that nanoparticles disperse throughout the tissues via the paracellular pathway.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental observations with fluorescent tracers and live imaging showing paracellular diffusion.

claim: The ubiquitous entry gate to within the cells' cytoplasm in coral tissues is macropinocytosis.
source: Then, the ubiquitous entry gate to within the cells' cytoplasm is macropinocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experimental approaches including TEM, inhibitor studies, and fluorescent tracer uptake.

claim: Most coral cells form large vesicles of 350–600 nm in diameter at their apical side, continuously internalizing their surrounding medium.
source: Most cells form large vesicles of 350–600 nm in diameter at their apical side, continuously internalizing their surrounding medium.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative analysis of vesicle sizes shown in Figure 7.

claim: Macropinocytosis in corals was confirmed using specific inhibitors of PI3K and actin polymerization.
source: Macropinocytosis was confirmed using specific inhibitors of PI3K and actin polymerization.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally with wortmannin (PI3K inhibitor) and latrunculin (actin inhibitor) in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: Nanoparticle internalization dynamics is size dependent and differs between tissues.
source: Nanoparticle internalization dynamics is size dependent and differs between tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through time course experiments with different sized dextrans shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Macropinocytosis is likely a major endocytic pathway in other anthozoan species.
source: Furthermore, we reveal that macropinocytosis is likely a major endocytic pathway in other anthozoan species.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by observations in Anemonia viridis and Corallium rubrum shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Gold nanoparticles were detected within large intracellular vesicles bigger than 200 nm in diameter in both ectodermal and endodermal layers.
source: Using transmission electron microscopy (Figure 2) we detected gold nanoparticles within large intracellular vesicles bigger than 200 nm in diameter, in both the ectodermal and the endodermal layers.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by TEM images in Figure 2.

claim: Dextran particles were never observed free in the cytoplasm.
source: Dextran particles were never observed free in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This observation is stated in the Results section based on TEM analysis.

claim: Electron micrographs showed large vesicle formation right below the apical membrane of both ectodermal and endodermal cells which is typical of macropinocytotic processes.
source: However, when osmium post-fixation was performed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), electron micrographs showed large vesicle formation right below the apical membrane of both ectodermal and endodermal cells which is typical of macropinocytotic processes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by TEM images in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: After 5 min, dextran molecules were visible at the apical surface of all epithelial layers except for the aboral calicoblastic ectoderm where the labeling appeared 10–20 min later.
source: After 5 min, dextran molecules were visible at the apical surface of all epithelial layers except for the aboral calicoblastic ectoderm where the labeling appeared 10–20 min later.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on time course experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The pattern of dextran uptake in the oral ectoderm appeared to be size-dependent, with preferential internalization of D3K versus D10K.
source: Importantly, the pattern of dextran uptake in the oral ectoderm appeared to be size-dependent, with preferential internalization of D3K versus D10K.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by observations in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: In both endoderms, dextran fluorescence in the cells was similar whatever the size of the dextran.
source: This was not the case within both endoderms where dextran fluorescence in the cells was similar whatever the size of the dextran (Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Video 1 and Figure 3.

claim: Both D3K and D10K dextrans co-localized in most vesicles in all cell layers, albeit with seemingly variable relative concentrations.
source: However, close inspection of the separate dextran confocal emission channels revealed that both dextrans co-localized in most vesicles in all cell layers, albeit with seemingly variable relative concentrations (ratio).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on confocal microscopy observations.

claim: After a 4 hr chase period, the dextran signal was more centrally positioned inside the cells, confirming an apical to basal progression in all tissues.
source: However, after a 4 hr chase period preceded by a wash (ie. dextran was no longer present in the incubation medium), the dextran signal was more centrally positioned inside the cells (compare with nuclei position), confirming an apical to basal progression in all tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on pulse-chase experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the oral epithelium, penetration of the D10K was delayed as compared with D3K.
source: Again (see above), in the oral epithelium, penetration of the D10K was delayed as compared with D3K (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: After the pulse1-chase-pulse2 experiment, dextran fluorescence from the first pulse was observable within the cells whereas the fluorescence of the dextran from the second pulse was only found at the apical side of the cells.
source: Whichever the epithelial cell layer considered, we show that after the pulse1-chase-pulse2 experiment, dextran fluorescence from the first pulse was observable within the cells whereas the fluorescence of the dextran from the second pulse was only found at the apical side of the cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on double pulse experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Dextran endocytosis occurs on the apical side of all cell layers.
source: Combined with the results of Figure 4, these results clearly demonstrate that dextran endocytosis occurs on the apical side of all cell layers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on double pulse experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Dextran diffuses along the paracellular pathway through septate junctions.
source: As was already observed with the tracer calcein in Tambutté et al. (2012), dextran diffuses along the paracellular pathway through septate junctions (Video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by live imaging in Video 2, with citation to previous work.

claim: Septate junctions are 15–20 nm in width and control the perm-selectivity of molecules.
source: Septate junctions are 15–20 nm in width and control the perm-selectivity of molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as established knowledge about septate junctions.

claim: In the aboral calicoblastic ectoderm, no particle uptake of latex beads was detected.
source: However, in the aboral calicoblastic ectoderm, no particle uptake was detected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on latex bead experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Barriers, likely represented by the septate junctions of the two aboral cell layers, prevent the paracellular diffusion of latex beads over 20 nm in diameter towards the ECM.
source: However, barriers, likely represented by the septate junctions of the two aboral cell layers (plus potentially the mesoglea), prevent the paracellular diffusion of latex beads over 20 nm in diameter towards the ECM and thus, prevent their access to the calicoblastic ectoderm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on latex bead experiments and represents an inference from the data.

claim: In the oral ectoderm, most vesicles were 350 to 800 nm in width, with or without the chase period.
source: In the oral ectoderm, most vesicles were 350 to 800 nm in width, with or without the chase period (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative analysis in Figure 7B.

claim: In the oral endoderm, after 4 hr of chasing, the size distribution shifted towards much larger vesicles (up to 1.5 µm in width), which possibly implies vesicle fusion with time and/or cytoplasm progression.
source: However, after 4 hr of chasing, the size distribution shifted towards much larger vesicles (up to 1.5 µm in width), which possibly implies vesicle fusion with time and/or cytoplasm progression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on quantitative analysis in Figure 7B, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Incubation with EIPA efficiently impaired the formation of macropinosomes in all cell layers.
source: Contrary to the DMSO control experiment (Figure 8A), incubation with EIPA efficiently impaired the formation of macropinosomes (Figure 8B) in all cell layers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: When incubated with 1 µM wortmannin, dextran uptake was impaired both quantitatively and qualitatively in every cell layer except for the aboral epitheliums.
source: When incubated with 1 µM wortmannin, dextran uptake was impaired both quantitatively and qualitatively (Figure 8C) in every cell layer except for the aboral epitheliums.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Vesicle formation was inhibited by Latrunculin (LatA) and inhibition was reversible.
source: Vesicle formation was also inhibited by Latrunculin (LatA) and inhibition was reversible (Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 9.

claim: Vesicle formation in S. pistillata was sensitive to EIPA, Wortmannin, and LatA, corroborating that vesicle formation follows the macropinocytosis route.
source: Thus, vesicle formation in S. pistillata was sensitive to EIPA, Wortmannin, and LatA, corroborating our previous results suggesting that vesicle formation follows the macropinocytosis route.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the inhibitor experiments.

claim: An F-actin 'cap' is associated with the forming macropinosomes at the apical side of the endodermal and calicoblastic cells.
source: After incubation with D3K for 15 min, we clearly observed an F-actin dent, that we termed 'cap', associated with the forming macropinosomes at the apical side of the endodermal and calicoblastic cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on phalloidin staining shown in Figure 10.

claim: The actin caps did not surround the dextran vesicles, at least in the initial stage of formation.
source: Importantly, these actin caps did not surround the dextran vesicles, at least in the initial stage of formation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on observations in Figure 10.

claim: The formation of an intracellular actin cap could create a depression at the surface of the plasma membrane provoking the engulfment of the extracellular liquid.
source: Our interpretation of the 3D reconstruction image stacks is that the formation of an intracellular actin cap could create a depression at the surface of the plasma membrane provoking the engulfment of the extracellular liquid.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the imaging data.

claim: Macropinocytosis is ubiquitous to most cells since every field observed with the microscope showed a labeling pattern similar to that shown in Video 1.
source: Our data suggest that macropinocytosis is ubiquitous to most cells since every field we observed with the microscope showed a labeling pattern similar to that shown in Video 1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on consistent observations across all experiments.

claim: Macropinocytosis is not specific to the scleractinian coral Stylophora pistillata since dextran internalisation was also observed in the sea anemone Anemonia viridis and in the red coral, Corallium rubrum.
source: Such a process is not specific to the scleractinian coral Stylophora pistillata since we also observed dextran internalisation in the sea anemone Anemonia viridis and in the red coral, Corallium rubrum.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on experiments with other anthozoan species.

claim: Macropinocytosis appears as an ubiquitous process found in different anthozoan species.
source: Macropinocytosis thus appears as an ubiquitous process found in different anthozoan species.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from observations across multiple species.

claim: Macropinocytosis is a ubiquitous endocytic pathway found in all the cell layers of the coral S. pistillata (Hexacorallia/Scleractinia).
source: Here, we show that macropinocytosis is a ubiquitous endocytic pathway found in all the cell layers of the coral S. pistillata (Hexacorallia/Scleractinia).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the main finding.

claim: Macropinocytosis is conserved in anthozoans since similar vesicles were observed in the sea-anemone Anemonia viridis (Hexacorallia/Actiniaria) and the red coral Corallium rubrum (Octocorallia/Scleraxonia).
source: Furthermore, we show that this pathway is conserved in anthozoans since we also observed similar vesicles in the sea-anemone Anemonia viridis (Hexacorallia/Actiniaria) and the red coral Corallium rubrum (Octocorallia/Scleraxonia)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on observations in multiple species.

claim: Hexacorallia and Octocorallia likely diverged more than 600 Mya.
source: Hexacorallia and Octocorallia are the two major subclasses of Anthozoa, which likely diverged more than 600 Mya (Kayal et al., 2018; Guzman et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the evolutionary timeline.

claim: Such a ubiquitous use of macropinocytosis was largely unexpected as this process is restricted to specialized cells in the sister group of Bilateria.
source: Such a ubiquitous use of macropinocytosis was largely unexpected as this process is restricted to specialized cells in the sister group of Bilateria.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison to bilaterians, drawing on general knowledge.

claim: Macropinocytosis is one of the endocytotic pathways that exists in eukaryotic cells, along with others such as clathrin-mediated endocytosis or phagocytosis.
source: Macropinocytosis is one of the endocytotic pathways that exists in eukaryotic cells, along with others such as clathrin-mediated endocytosis or phagocytosis (for more details see reviews Kerr et al., 2009; Canton, 2018; Lim and Gleeson, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to review articles.

claim: Macropinocytosis requires a dynamic actin skeleton essential for contractile motility.
source: Macropinocytosis requires a dynamic actin skeleton essential for contractile motility.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as established knowledge about macropinocytosis.

claim: Macropinocytosis differs from other types of endocytosis by its unique susceptibility to Na+/H+ exchanger inhibitors.
source: Macropinocytosis differs from other types of endocytosis by its unique susceptibility to Na+/H+ exchanger inhibitors (Cosson et al., 1989; Koivusalo et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Macropinocytosis is a Phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) dependent process in eukaryotes.
source: Macropinocytosis is also a Phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) dependent process in eukaryotes (Araki et al., 1996; Williams and Kay, 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The pharmacological approach suggests that the molecular processes leading to macropinocytosis are likely to be conserved throughout evolution.
source: Thus, although the initial shape of the macropinosome-forming membrane may differ in corals versus vertebrate cells or Dictyostelium, the pharmacological approach used here suggests that the molecular processes leading to macropinocytosis are likely to be conserved throughout evolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the inhibitor experiments.

claim: The size of the vesicles observed with the fluorescent fluid phase marker dextran is between 350 and 1500 nm, which is typical of macropinocytosis.
source: The size of the vesicles that we observed with the fluorescent fluid phase marker dextran is between 350 and 1500 nm, which is typical of macropinocytosis (Levin et al., 2015; Swanson, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the size range being typical of macropinocytosis.

claim: Studies in mammalian cells have shown that macropinocytosis can be induced in a variety of cell types by growth factors and other stimuli whereas dendritic cells and macrophages perform macropinocytosis constitutively.
source: Studies in mammalian cells have shown that macropinocytosis can be induced in a variety of cell types by growth factors and other stimuli whereas dendritic cells and macrophages perform macropinocytosis constitutively (Canton et al., 2016; Canton, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim about mammalian cells.

claim: Within 5 min, particles are detectable in the coelenteric cavity.
source: Our time course study shows that within 5 min, particles are detectable in the coelenteric cavity (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on time course experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: One possibility to explain the preferential endocytosis of smaller particles in the oral ectoderm is that bigger particles would be trapped or delayed by the mucus layer.
source: One possibility to explain the preferential endocytosis of smaller particles is that bigger particles would be trapped or delayed by this mucus layer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation to explain the size-dependent uptake.

claim: The ectodermal macropinosomes contain a heterogeneous medium with a fibrillary network (mucus-like) and the endodermal macropinosomes contain a homogeneous medium.
source: This is supported by the Transmission Electron Microscope observation of the content of the ectodermal versus endodermal macropinosomes (TEM observations): the former contain a heterogeneous medium with a fibrillary network (mucus-like) and the latter a homogeneous medium (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on TEM observations in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In A. viridis, macropinosome formation in the aboral endoderm takes 1 to 4 min.
source: In A. viridis, macropinosome formation in the aboral endoderm takes 1 to 4 min.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on experiments with A. viridis.

claim: Given the kinetics of vesicle formation as well as their size and number, macropinocytosis likely accounts for most of the fluid phase uptake in coral tissues, including the oral ectoderm.
source: Hence, given the kinetics of vesicle formation as well as their size and number, macropinocytosis likely accounts for most of the fluid phase uptake in coral tissues, including the oral ectoderm.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the experimental data.

claim: Macropinocytosis occurs in apparently the vast majority of coral cells.
source: Macropinocytosis occurs in apparently the vast majority of coral cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on widespread observations across all experiments.

claim: Particles are engulfed into large vesicles originating from the apical membrane of the cells.
source: Particles are engulfed into large vesicles originating from the apical membrane of the cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on experimental observations.

claim: Macropinosomes move towards the inner part of the cells, down to the basal side.
source: These macropinosomes then move towards the inner part of the cells, down to the basal side.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on pulse-chase experiments.

claim: Macropinosomes in the endodermal cells are notably bigger than those of the ectodermal cells.
source: Macropinosomes in the endodermal cells are notably bigger than those of the ectodermal cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on quantitative analysis in Figure 7.

claim: A likely explanation for larger macropinosomes in endodermal cells is that macropinosomes fuse during their progression.
source: A likely explanation is that in the endodermal cells, macropinosomes fuse during their progression.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation to explain the size difference.

claim: In vertebrate models, macropinosome fate after internalization varies depending on the cell type, as they can be recycled to the cell membrane or they can adopt degradative properties by fusing with lysosomes and undergoing a lysosome-dependent acidification.
source: In vertebrate models, macropinosome fate after internalization varies depending on the cell type, as they can be recycled to the cell membrane or they can adopt degradative properties by fusing with lysosomes and undergoing a lysosome-dependent acidification (Recouvreux and Commisso, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim about vertebrate models.

claim: The observation that diverse particles ranging in size from 1 to 200 nm are engulfed by most cell types suggests that exogenous particles such as DOM or particulate organic matter may enter these cells by macropinocytosis.
source: The observation that in corals, diverse particles ranging in size from 1 to 200 nm are engulfed by most cell types suggests that exogenous particles such as DOM or particulate organic matter may enter these cells by macropinocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference about the physiological role of macropinocytosis.

claim: The oral ectodermal cell layer was shown to directly absorb DOM sources from the surrounding sea water by its apical membrane.
source: The oral ectodermal cell layer was shown to directly absorb DOM sources from the surrounding sea water by its apical membrane (Schlichter, 1982; Sorokin, 1973), which corresponds to the side of macropinocytosis, and thus corroborates the fact that macropinocytosis could be the DOM feeding pathway in the oral ectoderm.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to previous studies.

claim: Bulk fluid absorption via macropinocytocis could form part of the mechanism for the uptake of photosynthates released in the coelenteric cavity.
source: Bulk fluid absorption via macropinocytocis could form part of the mechanism for the uptake of photosynthates released in the coelenteric cavity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation about the role of macropinocytosis in nutrient uptake.

claim: Individual coral cells, and more generally anthozoan cells, would have the capacity to use macropinocytosis for both auto-and heterotrophic feeding.
source: Hence, individual coral cells, and more generally anthozoan cells, would have the capacity to use macropinocytosis for both auto-and heterotrophic feeding.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference about the dual role of macropinocytosis.

claim: Mass and collaborators observed mineral particles within the calicoblastic cells, with sizes varying from 400 nm to 9.4 μm in diameter, 400 nm being the most frequent.
source: With regard to calcification, recently Mass and collaborators observed mineral particles within the calicoblastic cells, with sizes varying from 400 nm to 9.4 μm in diameter, 400 nm being the most frequent (Mass et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Mass et al. 2017.

claim: Sizes of the macropinosomes in the calicoblastic cells were in the same size range as in Clode and Marshall (2002), that is 350 to 800 nm.
source: In the present study, sizes of the macropinosomes in the calicoblastic cells were in the same size range as in Clode and Marshall (2002), that is 350 to 800 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section comparing the current findings to previous work.

claim: Apical to basal macropinocytosis is commonly observed during endocytotic events including micropinocytosis.
source: Of major interest, apical to basal macropinocytosis is commonly observed during endocytotic events including micropinocytosis (Shivas et al., 2010; Apodaca, 2001) and is the prevalent endocytic pathway in all coral tissues, including calicoblastic cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Calicoblastic cells capture the extracellular medium that is present at the interface between the cells and the skeleton (i.e. the ECM).
source: Thus, calicoblastic cells capture the extracellular medium that is present at the interface between the cells and the skeleton (i.e. the ECM).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the apical uptake observations.

claim: The composition of the ECM is different from seawater (higher pH, Ca and carbonate).
source: Taking this into account and the studies showing that the composition of the ECM is different from seawater (higher pH, Ca and carbonate [Sevilgen et al., 2019; Cai et al., 2016]), it is clear that 'calicoblastic' macropinosomes do not capture seawater from the medium but rather modified seawater.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim about ECM composition.

claim: Dextran labeled vesicles were never observed within the mesoglea, suggesting that vesicle passage from one tissue layer to the other does not occur.
source: Of note, we never observed dextran labeled vesicles within the mesoglea, suggesting that vesicle passage from one tissue layer to the other does not occur.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the absence of observations.

claim: Latex beads as large as 200 nm are able to enter the general coelenteric cavity, likely via the polyps' mouth.
source: In the present study, we show that latex beads as large as 200 nm are able to enter the general coelenteric cavity, likely via the polyps' mouth, as we observed their accumulation at the oral opening (not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on observations with latex beads.

claim: Large latex beads were apparently internalized with less efficiency than smaller nanoparticles such as dextrans.
source: Then, they are found within the cells, although large latex beads were apparently internalized with less efficiency than smaller nanoparticles such as dextrans (see Figures 4 and 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on comparison of Figures 4 and 6.

claim: It seems likely that the size of plastic fragments (micrometer vs nanometer) affects their internalization efficiency both at the coelenteric entry level and within the cells.
source: Thus, it seems likely that the size of plastic fragments (micrometer vs nanometer) also affects their internalization efficiency both at the coelenteric entry level and within the cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference about plastic particle uptake.

claim: Current studies on corals have so far only addressed the toxicological impact of micrometer sized and not nanometer sized plastics.
source: However, current studies on corals have so far only addressed the toxicological impact of micrometer sized (entry inside the organism) and not nanometer sized (entry into the cells) plastics (Reichert et al., 2018; Allen et al., 2017; Hankins et al., 2018; Rotjan et al., 2019), as it has been done in other organisms (e.g. Della Torre et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to current studies.

claim: Macropinocytosis allows internalization of nanoparticles of different sorts in all coral cells, and this endocytic pathway should be taken into account in future eco-toxicology studies.
source: Since macropinocytosis allows internalization of nanoparticles of different sorts in all coral cells, this endocytic pathway should now certainly be taken into account in future eco-toxicology studies.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a recommendation based on the findings.

claim: Anthozoans (corals and sea anemones) are simple organisms from a histological and anatomical point of view.
source: From a histological and anatomical point of view (Allemand et al., 2011; Tambutté et al., 2011), anthozoans (included in the phylum Cnidaria) are simple organisms
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The tissues of anthozoans are made up of two cell layers, the ectoderm and the endoderm separated by an acellular layer of mesoglea.
source: The tissues are made up of two cell layers, the ectoderm and the endoderm separated by an acellular layer of mesoglea.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as basic anatomical knowledge about anthozoans.

claim: Stony corals (scleractinians) represent the branch of anthozoans that synthetize a skeleton.
source: Stony corals (scleractinians) represent the branch of anthozoans that synthetize a skeleton.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as basic taxonomic knowledge.

claim: Most reef-building corals are symbiotic, hosting in their endodermal cells photosynthetic dinoflagellates (Symbiodiniaceae) from which they derive a large part of their organic nutrients.
source: Most reef-building corals are symbiotic, hosting in their endodermal cells photosynthetic dinoflagellates (Symbiodiniaceae) from which they derive a large part of their organic nutrients (Muscatine and Porter, 1977).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Transport of ions/molecules from one cell layer to another cell layer and between the two tissues has been shown to occur through two different pathways: a paracellular and a transcellular pathway.
source: Transport of ions/molecules from one cell layer to another cell layer and between the two tissues has been shown to occur through two different pathways: a paracellular and a transcellular pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as established knowledge about coral physiology.

claim: The paracellular pathway occurs through septate junctions.
source: The paracellular pathway (i.e. passing in between cells) occurs through septate junctions (Davy et al., 2012; Tambutté et al., 2012; Barott et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The paracellular pathway is selective and depends on the size and charge of each transported entity.
source: This paracellular pathway is selective and depends on the size and charge of each transported entity (Tambutté et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The permeability to ions is different between the oral and aboral tissues based on physiological experiments.
source: Based on physiological experiments, it has been shown that the permeability to ions is different between the oral and aboral tissues (Bénazet-Tambutté et al., 1996b).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The supply of ions to the ECM involves a transcellular pathway with channel/carriers located on the apical and basal membranes of the polarized calicoblastic cells.
source: The supply of ions to the ECM involves a transcellular pathway with channel/carriers located on the apical and basal membranes of the polarized calicoblastic cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as established knowledge about ion transport.

claim: Bicarbonate and calcium have been proposed to be transcellularly transported through carriers/channels.
source: For example, bicarbonate and calcium have been proposed to be transcellularly transported through these carriers/channels (Barott et al., 2015; Zoccola et al., 2015; Zoccola et al., 2004; Zoccola et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Some authors suggest that trans-cellular transport of vesicles occurs during the calcification process.
source: These processes have been poorly characterized in corals but some authors suggest that trans-cellular transport of vesicles occurs during the calcification process (Mass et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: It has been proposed that seawater is endocytosed into vesicles and enriched in carbonate ions in the calcifying cells, then transported and exocytosed in the ECM.
source: In these models, it has been proposed that seawater is endocytosed into vesicles and enriched in carbonate ions in the calcifying cells. These vesicles would then be transported and their content exocytosed in the ECM.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a proposed model from the literature.

claim: Macropinocytosis is a highly conserved process found from unicellular eukaryotes to metazoans.
source: Macropinocytosis is a highly conserved process found from unicellular eukaryotes to metazoans, similar to that of phagocytosis, although direct contact with the internalized material is not required as for phagocytosis (McNeil, 1981; Levin et al., 2015; Doherty and McMahon, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Macropinocytosis is an actin-driven process where plasma membrane ruffling and closing takes up surrounding extracellular fluids into large vesicles.
source: Macropinocytosis is an actin-driven process: plasma membrane ruffling and closing takes up surrounding extracellular fluids and its content into large vesicles, which may further fuse intracellularly with endosomal vesicles (Swanson, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: In humans, macropinocytosis can be constitutive or induced and has been involved in various cellular functions including antigen presentation, cell metabolism, cancer, pathogen entries, and therapeutics.
source: In humans, macropinocytosis can be constitutive or induced and has been involved in various cellular functions including antigen presentation, cell metabolism, as well as in cancer (increased nutrient uptake), pathogen entries (from viruses to protozoans), and therapeutics (drug entry gate) (Bloomfield and Kay, 2016; Levin et al., 2015; Recouvreux and Commisso, 2017; Canton et al., 2016; Canton, 2018; Yoshida et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2011; Lim and Gleeson, 2011; Commisso et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with multiple citations to support the claim.

claim: Macropinocytosis can be considered as the endocytic pathway allowing non-specific endocytosis of large nanoparticles, up to 5 µm in diameter.
source: Hence, macropinocytosis can be considered as the endocytic pathway allowing non-specific endocytosis of large nanoparticles, up to 5 µm in diameter (Swanson, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: In anthozoans, macropinocytosis has never been characterized despite its potential role in fluid uptake.
source: In anthozoans (which include sea anemones, gorgonians and corals), macropinocytosis has never been characterized despite its potential role in fluid uptake.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a knowledge gap.
